title_en: The Man Who Gave Machines a Mind
english_paragraphs: Born in June 1912, Alan Turing had a formidable intellect by his early twenties. In a paper read in November 1936, he outlined a "universal machine": a device able to execute any computation, given the right instructions. That abstract construct, rooted in mathematical logic, became the theoretical blueprint of the modern computer.

On 4 September 1939 he joined the classified codebreaking effort at Bletchley Park, leading work on naval Enigma, Germany's encryption machine. Polish mathematicians had deciphered Enigma by late 1932 and shared their insights with Britain and France in July 1939. His team's machines exploited them and, operational from March 1940, automated the laborious search for each day's rotor settings.

In October 1950, writing in the philosophy journal Mind, he posed a provocative question: "Can machines think?" He proposed a practical substitute, the imitation game, now widely called the Turing test. An interrogator exchanges typed messages with two concealed players, one human and one machine. If the interrogator cannot consistently distinguish them, the machine passes.

His exceptional wartime contribution did not protect him. On 31 March 1952 he was convicted of "gross indecency", the charge then used against gay men. He forfeited his security clearance and, to avert imprisonment, submitted to hormone injections. He died of cyanide poisoning on 7 June 1954. A coroner's inquest ruled it suicide, though some doubt it.

Recognition lagged. On 10 September 2009 Britain's prime minister publicly apologised, and on 24 December 2013 Turing was posthumously granted a royal pardon. On 23 June 2021, his birthday, a fifty-pound note bearing his portrait entered circulation. The country that prosecuted him put his face on its money.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 艾伦·图灵生于1912年6月，他已拥有**强大的**(formidable)**才智**(intellect)，二十出头时。在1936年11月宣读的一篇论文中，他**勾勒了**(outlined)一种“通用机器”：一种能**执行**(execute)任何**计算**(computation)的**装置**(device)，只要给出正确的指令。这一**抽象的**(abstract)**构想**(construct)**根源于**(rooted in)**数理**(mathematical)**逻辑**(logic)，后来成为了现代计算机的**理论**(theoretical)**蓝图**(blueprint)。

1939年9月4日，他加入了布莱切利园的**保密的**(classified)**破译工作**(codebreaking effort)，领导关于**海军**(naval)恩尼格玛密码机的工作，即德国的**加密**(encryption)机器。波兰数学家早在1932年底就已**破译了**(deciphered)恩尼格玛，并将他们的**深刻见解**(insights)（破解思路）于1939年7月告知了英国和法国。他团队（研制的）的机器**利用了**(exploited)这些见解和思路，并且从1940年3月起**投入运行**(operational)，**自动化了**(automated)每天搜寻**转子**(rotor)设置这项**耗时费力的**(laborious)工作。

1950年10月，他在**哲学**(philosophy)期刊《心灵》（Mind）上撰文，**提出了**(posed)一个**发人深省的**(provocative)问题——“机器能思考吗？”他**建议**(proposed)用一种**切实可行的**(practical)**替代办法**(substitute)取而代之，即模仿游戏，如今**普遍**(widely)称为图灵测试。一名**审问者**(interrogator)通过打字，与两个**隐藏起来的**(concealed)参与者交流，其中一个是人，一个是机器。如果审问者无法**始终如一地**(consistently)**区分出**(distinguish)二者，机器就算通过测试。

他**杰出的**(exceptional)**战时**(wartime)**贡献**(contribution)，并没有保护到他。1952年3月31日，他**被判定犯有**(convicted of)“严重猥亵”**罪**(convicted of)，这是当时用来惩治男同性恋者的罪名。他**被剥夺/丧失了**(forfeited)他的**安全许可**(security clearance)，并且为了**避免**(avert)**入狱**(imprisonment)，**被迫接受了**(submitted to)**激素**(hormone)**注射**(injections)。他死于**氰化物中毒**(cyanide poisoning)，1954年6月7日。**验尸官**(coroner)的死因调查裁定为**自杀**(suicide)，不过有人对此存疑。

（对于图灵的）**认可**(Recognition)**滞后了**(lagged)。2009年9月10日，英国首相**公开**(publicly)**道歉了**(apologised)；2013年12月24日，图灵在**死后**(posthumously)**被授予了**(was granted)皇室**赦免**(pardon)。2021年6月23日，也就是他的生日，印有他**肖像**(portrait)的五十英镑钞票开始**流通**(circulation)。**起诉**(prosecuted)他的国家，把他的头像印上了自己的钞票。

sentences.chinese_source: 一名**审问者**(interrogator)通过打字，与两个**隐藏起来的**(concealed)参与者交流，其中一个是人，一个是机器。

sentences.english: If the interrogator cannot consistently distinguish them, the machine passes.
sentences.chinese_source: 如果审问者无法**始终如一地**(consistently)**区分出**(distinguish)二者，机器就算通过测试。

sentences.english: His exceptional wartime contribution did not protect him.
sentences.chinese_source: 他**杰出的**(exceptional)**战时**(wartime)**贡献**(contribution)，并没有保护到他。

sentences.english: On 31 March 1952 he was convicted of "gross indecency", the charge then used against gay men.
sentences.chinese_source: 1952年3月31日，他**被判定犯有**(convicted of)“严重猥亵”**罪**(convicted of)，这是当时用来惩治男同性恋者的罪名。

sentences.english: He forfeited his security clearance and, to avert imprisonment, submitted to hormone injections.
sentences.chinese_source: 他**被剥夺/丧失了**(forfeited)他的**安全许可**(security clearance)，并且为了**避免**(avert)**入狱**(imprisonment)，**被迫接受了**(submitted to)**激素**(hormone)**注射**(injections)。

sentences.english: He died of cyanide poisoning on 7 June 1954.
sentences.chinese_source: 他死于**氰化物中毒**(cyanide poisoning)，1954年6月7日。

sentences.english: A coroner's inquest ruled it suicide, though some doubt it.
sentences.chinese_source: **验尸官**(coroner)的死因调查裁定为**自杀**(suicide)，不过有人对此存疑。

sentences.english: On 10 September 2009 Britain's prime minister publicly apologised, and on 24 December 2013 Turing was posthumously granted a royal pardon.
sentences.chinese_source: 2009年9月10日，英国首相**公开**(publicly)**道歉了**(apologised)；2013年12月24日，图灵在**死后**(posthumously)**被授予了**(was granted)皇室**赦免**(pardon)。

sentences.english: On 23 June 2021, his birthday, a fifty-pound note bearing his portrait entered circulation.
sentences.chinese_source: 2021年6月23日，也就是他的生日，印有他**肖像**(portrait)的五十英镑钞票开始**流通**(circulation)。

sentences.english: The country that prosecuted him put his face on its money.
sentences.chinese_source: **起诉**(prosecuted)他的国家，把他的头像印上了自己的钞票。

approved_summary: 1936年，图灵提出按指令执行各种计算的通用机器模型，为现代计算机奠定理论基础。
图灵团队借鉴波兰的破译成果，1940年用机器自动搜索德国海军密码机每天的设置，加速破译。
1950年，他提出模仿游戏：通过打字交谈，提问者若不能稳定分清人和机器，机器就通过测试。
1952年图灵因同性恋行为获罪，被取消涉密资格，为免入狱接受激素注射；1954年死于氰化物中毒。
其死被判为自杀，但有人质疑。英国2009年道歉、2013年给予身后赦免；2021年肖像登上50镑钞票。
